description.narrative:
Oxfam in Uganda has a strong track record in responding to disease outbreaks, including Ebola, Mpox, and cholera. The organisation responds through the adoption of integrated public health interventions in collaboration with the MoH, district health teams, and other health care partners. Our key strengths include: • WASH Interventions: Provision of safe water, water, operation and maintenanceof existing water supply systems, rehabilitation of boreholes, construction of permanent gender-segregated sanitation facilities, and promotion of hygiene practices to curb the spread of infectious diseases. • Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE): Working with community-based structures and local leaders to disseminate accurate information on Ebola prevention, symptoms, and available healthcare services as well as tracking community perceptions around the disease. • Infection Prevention and Control (IPC): Supporting health facilities with essential IPC materials such as handwashing stations, personal protective equipment (PPE), detergents/disinfectants for decontamination of soiled surfaces with blood, fluids in Ebola Treatment Units, disinfecting and desludging of filled up latrines, safe faecal sludge management at the treatment plant and waste management solutions. • Gender-Sensitive Programming: Ensuring that women, children, and marginalized groups have equal access to life-saving information and services. • Documentation and information sharing: Documentation of stories of change and best practices.
The initiative will complement, leverage and scale out the ongoing work being implemented by Oxfam through the Disaster Preparedness project in Mt Elgon region under a Consortium with Uganda Red cross Society and Caritas Tororo which is fundedby DG ECHO. The project activated a crisis Modifier of Euro 51,282 to support the ongoing Ebola response. This project aligns with the key pillars which include IPC-WaSH, Community Engagement <(>&<)> Risk Communication and Community-Based Surveillance within alimited scope of Mbale Business District.
2. Description of the Disaster
Uganda is currently experiencing an Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, with the index case of a health worker and first confirmed fatality recorded on January 29, 2025, in Kampala. The outbreak poses a severe public health threat, particularly in ten high-risk districts—Kampala, Wakiso, Mbale (city and district), Jinja (city and district), Iganga, Mukono, and Luwero—where the index case lived, worked, and sought medical treatment across multiple facilities. Given the movement of his family and contacts, the risk of widespread transmission remains high. An additional eight districts—Kasese, Buikwe, Mayuge, Namutumba, Kibuku, Budaka, Mpigi, and Mityana—have also been classifiedas high-risk areas due to population mobility and cross-district interactions. Ebola is a highly contagious and fatal disease, spreading primarily through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected individuals. The current outbreak threatens both public health and social stability, as unchecked transmission could lead to rising mortality, overwhelmed healthcare facilities, and severe socio-economic consequences. If the situation worsens, potential government-imposed lockdowns could disrupt livelihoods, increase food insecurity, and exacerbate malnutrition, particularly among vulnerable communities. Uganda's healthcare system, which heavily relies on donor funding—especially from organizations like USAID—faces significant challenges in managing a large-scale outbreak. Without immediate intervention, the country risks a prolonged crisis with devastating consequences for public health,economic stability, and community resilience. Urgent funding and collaboration with key stakeholders, including the Ministry of Health, WHO, and humanitarian organizations, are critical to containing the outbreak. Enhanced community engagement, epidemic preparedness, and resilience measures must be prioritized to break transmission chains, prevent further fatalities, and protect high-risk populations.
3. Impact of the Disaster
3.1 Impact on Population The Sudan Ebola outbreak in Uganda poses several significant impacts on the population which include: 1. High mortality risk with a fatality rate ranging from 40%-60%. This is mainly because there is no approved vaccine leading to fear and anxiety within the affected communities. 2. Healthcare systems are under pressure and face challenges of limited space to isolate patients, trace contacts and manage infections.The facilities may become overwhelmed thus reducing their capacity to treat other illnesses. 3. The fear of contracting the virus coupled with the death of loved ones leads to psychosocial stress, anxiety and stigma for survivors and their families. 4.Quarantine measures and movement restrictions can lead to social isolation, stigma, disruption of community life, livelihoods and social networks. Schools and workplaces may close temporarily to limit the spread of the virus thus affecting children’s education family incomes and generally social development.
3.2 Impact onResources The outbreak places immense pressure on basic services, which require government and international interventions to provide additional support. • The families may face displacement if homes are decontaminated or abandoned due to fear of infection. The caregivers for the sick or families under quarantine may suffer social isolation and stigma which reduces support from outside. • Increased water usage for handwashing and sanitation efforts may strain water resources. The areas without adequate access to clean water are at high risk for other diseases, compounding the crisis. • Handling and disposal of medical waste and contaminated materials become critical which stretches waste management systems beyond capacity. • Transportation of medical supplies and personnel may be hindered by travel restrictions. • The closure of marketplaces, schools and public gatherings places may limit access to essential services and goods. • Health facilities may be overwhelmed due to patient surges and staff shortages, isolation centres may be under resourced, and the health workers face high infection risks without sufficient PPEs.
4. Resulting Needs of the Affected Population Thereare critical needs for the affected population. These include: 1. Health care support needs: Access to timely medical care and treatment for infected individuals, adequate healthcare facilities including isolation centres and treatment units, sufficientpersonal protective equipment (PPEs) for health care workers and caregivers. 2. Sanitation and hygiene needs: Access to clean water for handwashing and hygiene practices to reduce transmission. Increased availability of sanitation supplies, including soap, disinfectantsand waste disposal systems plus proper medical waste disposal facilities to prevent contamination. 3. Access to safe Water: There is need for expansion of clean water sources to meet increased demand and emergency water distribution in areas with limited access. This is required to improve Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Capacities. 5. Public Awareness and Education Raising public awareness and providing accurate information are essential to promoting hygiene practices, countering misinformation, and reducing stigma associated with Ebola. Community engagement plays a crucial role in fostering trust and encouraging cooperation with public healthmeasures. 6. Promoting the Adoption of Protective Behaviors at the Community Level To effectively contain the outbreak, it is vitalto encourage communities to adopt protective behaviors, including proper hygiene practices, early reporting of symptoms, and adherence to infection prevention and control measures. Engaging local leaders, healthcare workers, and community volunteers will help reinforce these behaviors and ensure a coordinated response.
7. Initial Oxfam Response
Oxfam in Consortium with Uganda Redcross Society and Caritas Tororo is currently implementing an ECHO funded initiative to strengthen disaster preparedness and response in the greater Mt Elgon sub-region. Through the initiative, a crisis Modifier worth Euro 51,282 has been activated for 3 months (1st February to 30th April 2025) to support Ebola response within a limited scope of Mbale City and District. The project aligns with the key Ebola response plan pillars of the Ministry of Health (MOH) which include: IPC-WaSH: Through installing handwashing stations in key locations (quarantine centers, health facilities, public areas) and procure and distribute proper PPEs for exposed and hygiene practices for health workers, URCS staff, volunteers and the community village health teams Community Engagement <(>&<)> Risk Communication: by conducting community sensitization through door-to-door outreach, mobile cinema, radio broadcasts, and public posters and usesocial media and local leaders to spread accurate information about Ebola prevention. Community-Based Surveillance: trough Support refresher training for local volunteers and VHTs, health workers to monitor symptoms and report suspected cases and Deploying Community Based Structures teams to strengthen data collection data and provide feedback to improve surveillance efforts.
8. Proposed Response
6.1 Aim and Outcomes The aim of this project is to reduce mortality and morbidity caused by Ebola outbreak in very high-riskareas of Mbale city and Mbale district local government in Mt. Elgon sub-region. This will be achieved through enhanced community engagement, epidemic preparedness, and resilience-building measures.
Outcome .1: Improved coordination <(>&<)> leadership at all levels (municipalities, divisions, community, district <(>&<)> national) for Ebola prevention and response
• Facilitating DTF coordination meetings to share Epidemic intervention strategies, updates on epidemic status • Conduct 02 joint Infection Prevention [IPC] monitoring of facilities with the stakeholders, IPC committees using developed audit tools, WASHFIT and other checklists
Outcome.2: Strengthened infection prevention and control (IPC) measures at Offices, Ebola treatment ETU's, health centre facilities and schools in Mbale City and District.
• Installation of bulk Handwashing facilities at health facilities, markets, schools and ETUs • Purchase/provision of latrine cleaning tools (hard brush, Metallic bucket, Rubber squeezer) and detergents (liquid soap), jik for ETU/Isolation centres and schools. • Procurement of chlorine - Calcium hypochlorite (stable bleaching powder)of “HTH” equivalent quality in granular or powder with 65% Active Chorine) for ETU/Isolation centres • Procure and distribute dignity kits for women and girls in ETU/ isolation centres • Support Desludging of filled up latrine facilities at ETU and other Ebola holding centres • Construction of 4units emergency sanitary facility (temporary latrines and bath shelters) at the ETU's/quarantine/isolation centres • Construction of 1 block of 2 stances gender sensitive drainable latrines at ETU centre. • Repair and rehabilitation of community water points (Rehabilitation of handpumps) • Provision of soap for hand washing to highly vulnerable community members (Elderly, PWDs, VHTs etc) • Procurement and distribution waste collection bin
Outcome .3: Increased public awareness and early health-seeking behavior for Ebola prevention and management
• Support, translation, testing, production and distribution of IECs material (flyers and posters+B50:B54) with Ebola prevention messages to address the protective behaviors in close collaboration with the community, MoH.various local languages), • Public education / sensitization through mass media awareness such as radio talk shows or drama or cinemas (1 campaign per month for 3 districts) • Conduct community dialogue meeting with key stakeholders such as religious leaders, cultural leaders on Ebola Prevention and control as well enhancement of awareness creation in public gatherings (churches and mosques). • Procurement ofTransmission Megaphones + batteries with automatic sirens to support VHT's in mobilization. • Support mapping of hot spots and preparation of community action plans by community structures • Documentation and dissemination of lessons learnt for Uganda EVD Response • Conduct Post distribution Monitoring
6.2 Target Area and Population Target population of 17,423 which is 3% of the total population of Mbale and Mbale City under the age groups of (0 – 65 years) as per the population census of 2024 will be targeted with the intervention. The project will directly support vulnerable populations at high risk of infection, including: • Health workers and frontline responders, ensuring they have proper Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures. Oxfam staff and partners (ECHO fundedConsortium including Uganda Red Cross Society-URCS; Caritas Tororo) will be specifically targeted. • Women and children, who are athigher risk due to caregiving roles and limited access to healthcare. • People with disabilities and the elderly, ensuring inclusion in preparedness and response interventions. NB: The project wil target 17, 423 direct participants in Mbale and Mbale city.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
